conventions.convention: The one-letter exponent functions use finite nonempty alphabets, natural logarithms, ρ≥0 for E0, ρ≥1 for E0x, and 0^a=0 for a>0.
Reliability uses R>0, M_n=ceil(exp(nR)), deterministic codes, separate average and maximal errors, separate liminf and limsup exponents, and −ln(0)=+∞.
V(P,W) is the input-weighted conditional information variance, omitting zero-weight rows; Vmin and Vmax optimize over capacity-achieving input laws and are measured in nats squared.
The constant-composition/Gallager identity holds after maximizing over input laws; no pointwise-in-P identity is asserted.
The dependence-testing threshold is ln((M−1)/2), with strict threshold passage and a lowest-index decoder rule; the resulting guarantee concerns average error.
In the meta-converse, beta_epsilon constrains rejection under the true first law and minimizes acceptance under the auxiliary second law.
The sphere-packing converse assumes AC and Countable Choice, restricts auxiliary channel rows to the corresponding W-row supports, and requires R>R_infinity; it asserts no endpoint result.
The normal approximation assumes AC, a fixed finite unconstrained no-feedback DMC, fixed 0<epsilon<1/2, and Vmin>0; its remainder is O(ln n) for both error criteria.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite DMC W, every input law attaining C(W)=max_P I(P,W) induces the same output law Q*. This output law is unique even when the capacity-achieving input law is not.
Let W be a finite DMC, C=C(W), and Π={P:I(P,W)=C}. There is α>0, depending on W, such that every input law P satisfies C−I(P,W)≥α dist_2(P,Π)^2.
Assume AC. For independent finite-support mean-zero real X_1,…,X_n with total variance σ²>0, the uniform CDF error of (sum_i X_i)/σ from Φ is at most 1088 sum_i E|X_i|³/σ³.
For a finite DMC and every ρ>0, max_P inf_{V:V_x≪W_x}{sum_x P(x)D(V_x||W_x)+ρ I_P(V)}=max_P E0(ρ,P), omitting zero-weight rows. At ρ=0 both sides are zero under the stated conventions.
For any input law on a finite-DMC block channel and M≥2, a deterministic M-message code exists with average error at most E exp(−[imath(X^n;Y^n)−ln((M−1)/2)]_+). For M=1 a zero-error code exists.
Let d≥1, Δ_d be the probability simplex, M:R^d→R^r linear, and F={q∈Δ_d:Mq=b} nonempty. There is finite H such that dist_2(p,F)≤H||Mp−b||_2 for every p∈Δ_d.
For a finite DMC, P↦E0(ρ,P) for each ρ≥0 and P↦E0x(ρ,P) for each ρ≥1 are finite and continuous on the input simplex and attain finite maxima. E0(0,P)=0.
For every CAID P, each positive-mass input has conditional information-density mean C(W), and the unconditional information-density variance equals V(P,W).
